topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes students, introduces the lecturer, and outlines the core learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetic Predisposition, Environmental Risk, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce fundamental concepts of cancer development, debating the balance between intrinsic bad luck, genetic background, and environmental factors using epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Direct and Metabolically Activated Carcinogens: Pathogens, Radiation, and Chemicals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore specific environmental mutagens—including viral/bacterial pathogens, UV radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical agents—and the mechanisms by which they induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, focusing on tumor promoters, chronic inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental timing in host tissues.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental and statistical methodologies used to establish carcinogenicity—including mutational signatures, epidemiology, animal bioassays, and the Ames test—along with concluding thoughts on risk appraisal.
